summary: Clamp is correct: Math.min runs after positiveInt, so the fallback and invalid values still give 20 and the store's offset uses the capped size, so page walking stays consistent. Read src/server.mjs, src/store.mjs, src/client.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs, test/helpers.mjs and AGENTS.md in full, and grepped pageSize/MAX_PAGE_SIZE. The only caller is client.all(), which uses pageSize=50 (under the cap) and stops on items.length/total, so it is not broken. All 7 tests pass. The one gap is that the new test does not prove the list itself is cut to 100.

findings.issue: With only 3 notes, `items.length === 3` would also pass without the cap. The test only checks the echoed `pageSize` field, not that the server actually returns at most 100 items (the point of the change: one request cannot ask for the whole table). It also does not check the boundaries (pageSize=100 stays at 100, pageSize=101 becomes 100).
findings.fix: Seed 101+ notes (for example 105) and assert `r.body.items.length === 100` and `r.body.total === 105`. Optionally also assert that `/notes?pageSize=100` returns pageSize 100 and `/notes?page=2&pageSize=1000` returns the last 5 items.

findings.issue: The cap is silent. An outside caller that asks for pageSize > 100 and treats `items.length < requestedPageSize` as the last page will now stop after the first 100 items and lose data. The response shape keeps its fields, and the capped value does come back in `pageSize`, but the page size a caller can get has changed. AGENTS.md treats the response as a contract, and the cap is not documented anywhere.
findings.fix: Document the 100 cap (README or AGENTS.md, and a comment next to client.all). Decide whether a pageSize over the limit should get a 400 JSON error instead of being silently capped. If silent capping stays, note that callers must use `total` or the returned `pageSize`, not the pageSize they asked for.

pre_existing.code:
const body = await readJson(req)
        return send(res, 201, store.create(user, body.text))
pre_existing.issue: A body of `null` (valid JSON) makes readJson resolve null, so `body.text` throws a TypeError and the request gets a 500 instead of a 4xx JSON error. This breaks the house rule that a bad request returns a 4xx. The same applies to any JSON body that is not an object and whose property access throws.
No limit on body size. A client can stream a huge body into memory before the 500-character text check runs.
Dead code: no route calls `remove`, and it has no owner check, so any future route wired to it would let one user delete another user's note.
